scenario: Irene is a mid-career product manager at a major financial firm. She leads cross-functional teams but feels slowed down by developer bottlenecks. She wants to 'speak AI' fluently and use Vibe Coding to lead faster innovation cycles within her organization.
expectations: Actionable, time-efficient learning suited for working professionals
Hands-on AI prototyping without heavy coding prerequisites
Tools to communicate AI-driven insights to non-technical stakeholders

phases.title: Phase 1 | Awareness
actions: Reads about AI-driven product management trends on LinkedIn.
Finds NC State’s Entrepreneurial AI course while exploring leadership upskilling options.
Discusses internal innovation goals with senior leadership.
pains: Dependency on developer teams to test ideas.
Unclear path to adopting AI tools within corporate constraints.

feelings.quote: I’m ready to lead innovation, not wait for it.

opportunities: Showcase managers who accelerated product timelines using AI.
Offer a short quiz to match course content to corporate innovation goals.

phases.title: Phase 2 | Consideration
actions: Compares NC State’s program to similar executive education offerings.
Downloads a sample syllabus to gauge workload.
Attends a live info session hosted by the course instructor.
pains: Unsure how technical the course content will be.

feelings.quote: If this bridges business and tech, I’m all in.

opportunities: Highlight portfolio-ready deliverables and AI workflow documentation.
Provide a pre-course diagnostic to personalize her learning plan.

phases.title: Phase 3 | Enrollment
actions: Registers through NC State’s continuing ed portal.
Schedules weekly time blocks for 90-minute sprints.
Downloads tool setup guides for VS Code and ChatGPT.
pains: Worries about balancing course work with job demands.
Concern about the technical setup process.

feelings.quote: This is a bold move—but I’m committed.

opportunities: Provide onboarding videos for quick tech setup.
Send motivational progress updates via email.

phases.title: Phase 4 | Engagement
actions: Applies AI to prototype a reporting dashboard for internal teams.
Documents her workflow as a Pattern Card.
Presents her demo to upper management.
pains: Occasional confusion about AI prompts and integrations.

feelings.quote: I finally understand how to turn strategy into execution.

opportunities: Provide templates for efficiency metrics tracking.
Create a spotlight series featuring executive learners’ outcomes.
